question: A tree is 10 m in front of a convex mirror of focal length 2.5 m. Its image is formed:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2.0 m behind mirror.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A convex mirror always forms a virtual, diminished, and erect image of the object placed in front of it.
 
• The **focal length of a convex mirror is always positive**, which means that the mirror is diverging in nature.
 
• Using the mirror formula,** 1/f = 1/v + 1/u,** where **f **is the focal length, **u **is the object distance, and **v** is the image distance, we can find the image distance for the given problem.
 
• Here, the **object distance is -10 m **and the **focal length is 2.5 m**.
 
• By substituting these values in the formula, we get **v = 2.0 m**, which means that the **image is formed 2.0 m behind the mirror.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A convex mirror is also known as a diverging mirror as it diverges the light rays.
 
• The image formed by a convex mirror is always virtual, diminished, and upright.
 
• The principal focus of a convex mirror is a point on the principal axis where the light rays appear to diverge from after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• The focal length of a convex mirror is always negative, and it is equal to half of the radius of curvature of the mirror.
